polite: dochira kara irasshatta n desu ka?
politeJa: どちらからいらっしゃったんですか？
english: where are you from?; where did you come from?
use: Asked when meeting a newcomer, usually meaning which country; answer with the place plus kara (kanada kara).

example.romaji: nee, doko kara kita no? amerika?
example.ja: ねえ、どこから来たの？アメリカ？
example.english: Hey, where are you from? America?

examplePolite.romaji: sumimasen, dochira kara irasshatta n desu ka?
examplePolite.ja: すみません、どちらからいらっしゃったんですか？
examplePolite.english: Excuse me, where are you from?

notes: Can also mean where you've just come from today; context decides.

english: I'm from ...; I grew up in ...
use: Your answer to shusshin doko?; put the country, city or prefecture first.

example.romaji: kanada no toronto shusshin da yo.
example.ja: カナダのトロント出身だよ。
example.english: I'm from Toronto, in Canada.

examplePolite.romaji: kanada no toronto shusshin desu.
examplePolite.ja: カナダのトロント出身です。
examplePolite.english: I'm from Toronto, in Canada.

politeJa: ご出身はどちらですか？
english: where are you from?; where did you grow up?
use: Asks where someone was born and raised; between Japanese people it usually means which prefecture.

example.romaji: shusshin doko? watashi wa oosaka.
example.ja: 出身どこ？私は大阪。
example.english: Where are you from? I'm from Osaka.

examplePolite.romaji: goshusshin wa dochira desu ka? watashi wa oosaka desu.
examplePolite.ja: ご出身はどちらですか？私は大阪です。
examplePolite.english: Where are you from? I'm from Osaka.

notes: Doko kara kita no? is the vaguer 'which country' version.

english: whereabouts in ...?
use: The follow-up after someone names a country or city; answer with a nearby big city or ... no chikaku (near ...).

example.romaji: igirisu no dono hen? rondon?
example.ja: イギリスのどの辺？ロンドン？
example.english: Whereabouts in England? London?

examplePolite.romaji: igirisu no dono hen desu ka? rondon desu ka?
examplePolite.ja: イギリスのどの辺ですか？ロンドンですか？
examplePolite.english: Whereabouts in England? London?

notes: Hen also works for vague places on its own: kono hen (around here).

english: where's your hometown?
use: Casual; mostly asked between Japanese people who've moved to a city for work or study.

example.romaji: jimoto doko? natsu ni kaeru no?
example.ja: 地元どこ？夏に帰るの？
example.english: Where's home for you? Going back for the summer?

examplePolite.romaji: jimoto wa dochira desu ka? natsu ni kaerimasu ka?
examplePolite.ja: 地元はどちらですか？夏に帰りますか？
examplePolite.english: Where's your hometown? Are you going back for the summer?

notes: Jimoto also means your local area: jimoto no tomodachi (friends from back home).

english: I live in ...
use: Answer to doko ni sunderu no?; name the city, area or nearest station.

example.romaji: ima wa shibuya no chikaku ni sunderu yo.
example.ja: 今は渋谷の近くに住んでるよ。
example.english: I live near Shibuya now.

examplePolite.romaji: ima wa shibuya no chikaku ni sunde imasu.
examplePolite.ja: 今は渋谷の近くに住んでいます。
examplePolite.english: I live near Shibuya now.

notes: Always the -te iru form (sunderu) for where you live now, and ni, not de.

kana: いまどこにすんでるの？
polite: ima dochira ni osumai desu ka?
politeJa: 今どちらにお住まいですか？
english: where do you live now?
use: Asked once you've said where you're from, to get the current city or neighbourhood.

example.romaji: ima doko ni sunderu no? kono hen?
example.ja: 今どこに住んでるの？この辺？
example.english: Where do you live now? Around here?

examplePolite.romaji: ima dochira ni osumai desu ka? kono hen desu ka?
examplePolite.ja: 今どちらにお住まいですか？この辺ですか？
examplePolite.english: Where do you live now? Around here?

notes: Osumai is the set polite word for someone's home; doko ni sunde imasu ka? is fine too.

english: do you live on your own?; living alone?
use: A common follow-up to where you live; answer un, hitorigurashi, or say who you live with.

example.romaji: e, hitorigurashi? ryouri toka suru no?
example.ja: え、一人暮らし？料理とかするの？
example.english: Oh, you live on your own? Do you cook and stuff?

examplePolite.romaji: hitorigurashi desu ka? ryouri toka shimasu ka?
examplePolite.ja: 一人暮らしですか？料理とかしますか？
examplePolite.english: Do you live on your own? Do you cook?

english: I live with my parents; I live at home

example.romaji: mada jikka ni sunderu n da. raku da yo.
example.ja: まだ実家に住んでるんだ。楽だよ。
example.english: I still live with my parents. It's easy.

examplePolite.romaji: mada jikka ni sunde iru n desu. raku desu yo.
examplePolite.ja: まだ実家に住んでいるんです。楽ですよ。
examplePolite.english: I still live with my parents. It's easy.

notes: Jikka is your parents' home; jikka ni kaeru means going home to visit them.

english: I work at ...; I work in ...
use: The basic answer to where you work; put the place or company before de.

example.romaji: ekimae no kafe de hataraiteru yo.
example.ja: 駅前のカフェで働いてるよ。
example.english: I work at the café by the station.

examplePolite.romaji: ekimae no kafe de hataraite imasu.
examplePolite.ja: 駅前のカフェで働いています。
examplePolite.english: I work at the café by the station.

notes: Hataraku takes de for the place, but sumu takes ni.

english: what kind of work is it?; what do you do?
use: Follow-up when someone mentions their job or company; answer with a role or field.

example.romaji: kaishain na n da. donna shigoto?
example.ja: 会社員なんだ。どんな仕事？
example.english: Oh, you work for a company. What kind of work?

examplePolite.romaji: kaishain na n desu ne. donna oshigoto desu ka?
examplePolite.ja: 会社員なんですね。どんなお仕事ですか？
examplePolite.english: Oh, you work for a company. What kind of work do you do?

notes: Oshigoto adds polite o- when it's someone else's job.

english: I work for a company; I'm an office worker
use: The everyday vague answer about your job; expect donna shigoto? next.

example.romaji: futsuu no kaishain da yo. jimu no shigoto.
example.ja: 普通の会社員だよ。事務の仕事。
example.english: Just an ordinary office worker. Admin work.

examplePolite.romaji: futsuu no kaishain desu. jimu no shigoto desu.
examplePolite.ja: 普通の会社員です。事務の仕事です。
examplePolite.english: I'm just an ordinary office worker. I do admin work.

notes: Sarariiman is a near-synonym, used for men.

kana: どこではたらいてるの？
polite: dochira de hataraite iru n desu ka?
politeJa: どちらで働いているんですか？
english: where do you work?
use: Asks for the company or place; people often answer with the industry instead of a company name.

example.romaji: ima doko de hataraiteru no? mada ginkou?
example.ja: 今どこで働いてるの？まだ銀行？
example.english: Where are you working now? Still at the bank?

examplePolite.romaji: ima dochira de hataraite iru n desu ka?
examplePolite.ja: 今どちらで働いているんですか？
examplePolite.english: Where are you working now?

notes: Shigoto nani shiteru no? (what do you do?) is the more common opener.

kana: 〜かんけいのしごとをしてる
polite: ... kankei no shigoto o shite imasu
english: I work in ...; I do something to do with ...
use: A handy vague answer when you don't want to explain your job; put the field first (ryokou kankei, kinyuu kankei).

example.romaji: ryokou kankei no shigoto o shiteru yo.
example.ja: 旅行関係の仕事をしてるよ。
example.english: I work in travel.

examplePolite.romaji: ryokou kankei no shigoto o shite imasu.
examplePolite.ja: 旅行関係の仕事をしています。
examplePolite.english: I work in travel.

notes: Casual speech often drops the o: ... kankei no shigoto shiteru.

src: 日本語勉強してるんだ
ja: 日本語勉強してるんだ
kana: にほんごべんきょうしてるんだ
polite: nihongo o benkyou shite iru n desu
politeJa: 日本語を勉強しているんです
english: I'm learning Japanese
use: Tells people why your Japanese is limited; the n da makes it an explanation that invites patience.

example.romaji: ima nihongo benkyou shiteru n da. yukkuri hanashite.
example.ja: 今日本語勉強してるんだ。ゆっくり話して。
example.english: I'm learning Japanese at the moment. Talk slowly for me.

examplePolite.romaji: ima nihongo o benkyou shite iru n desu. yukkuri hanashite kudasai.
examplePolite.ja: 今日本語を勉強しているんです。ゆっくり話してください。
examplePolite.english: I'm learning Japanese at the moment. Please speak slowly.

english: do you speak English?; can you speak English?
use: You'll hear it from people keen to switch to English; to keep practising, answer with nihongo de hanasou.

example.romaji: gomen, eigo hanaseru? nihongo mada heta de.
example.ja: ごめん、英語話せる？日本語まだ下手で。
example.english: Sorry, do you speak English? My Japanese is still bad.

examplePolite.romaji: sumimasen, eigo hanasemasu ka? nihongo ga mada heta de.
examplePolite.ja: すみません、英語話せますか？日本語がまだ下手で。
examplePolite.english: Excuse me, do you speak English? My Japanese is still bad.

notes: Hanaseru is the 'can' form of hanasu.

english: I taught myself; self-taught
use: Answer to where or how you learned something, Japanese or a hobby like guitar.

example.romaji: gakkou wa itte nai. zenbu dokugaku da yo.
example.ja: 学校は行ってない。全部独学だよ。
example.english: No classes. I taught myself all of it.

examplePolite.romaji: gakkou ni wa itte imasen. zenbu dokugaku desu.
examplePolite.ja: 学校には行っていません。全部独学です。
examplePolite.english: I haven't taken classes. I taught myself all of it.

notes: Dokugaku de benkyou shita = I studied it on my own.

src: 日本語どこで勉強したの？
ja: 日本語どこで勉強したの？
kana: にほんごどこでべんきょうしたの？
romaji: nihongo doko de benkyou shita no?
polite: nihongo wa doko de benkyou shita n desu ka?
politeJa: 日本語はどこで勉強したんですか？
english: where did you learn your Japanese?
use: Said to you by Japanese people, usually as a compliment; answer with a place, or dokugaku (self-taught).

example.romaji: sugoi ne! nihongo doko de benkyou shita no?
example.ja: すごいね！日本語どこで勉強したの？
example.english: Wow! Where did you learn your Japanese?

examplePolite.romaji: sugoi desu ne! nihongo wa doko de benkyou shita n desu ka?
examplePolite.ja: すごいですね！日本語はどこで勉強したんですか？
examplePolite.english: That's impressive! Where did you learn your Japanese?

politeJa: 日本語で話しましょう
english: let's talk in Japanese
use: Ask for this when someone switches to English to help you; it's how you keep getting practice.

example.romaji: renshuu shitai kara, nihongo de hanasou yo.
example.ja: 練習したいから、日本語で話そうよ。
example.english: I want the practice, so let's talk in Japanese.

examplePolite.romaji: renshuu shitai node, nihongo de hanashimashou.
examplePolite.ja: 練習したいので、日本語で話しましょう。
examplePolite.english: I'd like the practice, so let's speak Japanese.

notes: Softer: nihongo de hanashite mo ii? (is it OK if we speak Japanese?).

src: 日本に来てどのぐらい？
ja: 日本に来てどのぐらい？
kana: にほんにきてどのぐらい？
polite: nihon ni kite dono gurai desu ka?
politeJa: 日本に来てどのぐらいですか？
english: how long have you been in Japan?
use: One of the first questions you'll get; answer with a length of time plus ni naru (ninen ni naru).

example.romaji: nihon ni kite dono gurai? nihongo umai ne.
example.ja: 日本に来てどのぐらい？日本語うまいね。
example.english: How long have you been in Japan? Your Japanese is good.

examplePolite.romaji: nihon ni kite dono gurai desu ka? nihongo ga ojouzu desu ne.
examplePolite.ja: 日本に来てどのぐらいですか？日本語がお上手ですね。
examplePolite.english: How long have you been in Japan? Your Japanese is very good.

notes: Also said dono kurai; same thing.
